title: SLI drift sandbox and staged remediation playbook for inference tail-latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: We are observing intermittent SLI drift in p95/p99 tail-latency for chat/generation endpoints during bursty traffic patterns. Existing error budget runbooks are generic and trigger broad rollbacks which are costly. Goal: create a reproducible SLI-drift sandbox and a staged remediation playbook that targets inference-specific mitigations (batching tweaks, KV cache warming, model variant fallback) before broad rollbacks. The deliverable is a documented playbook, automated detection-to-remediation pipeline in the Console, and a small sandbox cluster + experiment harness for PM/Eng to run reproducible regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Sandbox: a lightweight isolated inference cluster (can be ephemeral) and load profile generator that reproduces observed tail-latency patterns
Detection rules: Console rule groups that reliably flag p95/p99 drift with contextual signals (queue depth, average batch size, recent model changes)

Playbook steps: documented staged remediations (1. dynamic batch target adjust, 2. KV cache prefetch, 3. switch to lower-latency quantized variant, 4. route to dedicated pool) with roll-forward and rollback criteria
Automation: a runbook workflow in Console that can execute the first two mitigations automatically and escalate to manual for model variant switch
Metrics: dashboards and alerts show reduced MTTD/MTTR in experiments vs baseline and no increase in error rate after mitigation
Safety: fallbacks include canary windows and automatic revert if quality regressions exceed threshold defined in eval suite
approach: 1) Build a compact sandbox infra template (k8s yaml + small GPU pool) and a replay driver that replays production ingress profiles. 2) Instrument the Console to capture candidate signals for drift (batching stats, KV hit rate, kernel queue depth). 3) Draft staged remediation sequences ranked by cost/latency impact. 4) Implement automation for the lowest-risk steps (batch tuning + cache warming) via the Console runbook engine. 5) Run 3 controlled experiments, capture telemetry, refine playbook, and hand off to oncall/Reliability stewards.
risks: Automated mitigations could mask root cause and lead to repeated interventions without fix
Sandbox may not faithfully reproduce rare network/gpu contention modes seen in scale
Switching to quantized variants could introduce subtle quality regressions for edge prompts
Integration with Console runbook APIs may require additional auth/infra work (ENG scope)
Customer-facing incidents may still require fast human decision-making beyond automation
tasks: Define sandbox infra template and cost budget
Implement replay driver and attach to recent p99 incident traces
Design detection rules and test on historical windows
Draft playbook prose and verification tests
Build Console runbook actions for batch tuning and cache warming
Coordinate with ENG for quantized model variant gating and canary policy
Run three scheduled experiments and capture learnings
Publish playbook in Confluence and link to Console runbook
